title: BPO Assurance-Case Cross-Walk
description: Canonical record for one verification project's alignment against the BPO catalogue. This schema is PUBLISHED BY BPO but INSTANTIATED DOWNSTREAM: a crosswalk is an artifact of the verification project that produced the evidence, and it points *up* at the ontology. BPO therefore hosts this contract and a synthetic fixture, but hosts no real case study — a catalogue that carried one subject's evidence would invert the dependency. The schema's purpose is to make it structurally impossible to launder a local tool result into an ontology-level verification claim: `proof_transfer` is pinned to `none`, evidence CLASS is recorded separately from the CLAIMS made about it (so `schema/validate_refs.py` can cross-check them), and the declared ledger/summary counts are recomputed from the data at build time. Nothing in this schema may be specific to any one protocol, tool, or project.

id.description: Stable handle for this crosswalk release, e.g. 'example-lending-b-0-1-0'.

version.description: SemVer of this crosswalk document, independent of both the subject's version and the BPO baseline.

name.description: The system under verification. Free text: this schema takes no position on what kind of system it is.

revision.description: Exact pinned revision of the subject the evidence was produced against. Without this, no result in the document is reproducible.

Exact BPO revision the alignment was decided against. Alignment decisions are only meaningful relative to a corpus snapshot; a later BPO change becomes an explicit crosswalk delta rather than a silent reinterpretation.

property_count.description: Size of the BPO corpus at that revision, recorded so a reviewer can tell whether 'no exact match' meant 24 records or 240.

local_ledger.description: Author-DECLARED sizes of the local obligation and assumption ledgers. schema/validate_refs.py RECOMPUTES both from the arrays below and fails the build on disagreement, so a truncated or padded document cannot pass silently.

alignment_summary.description: Author-DECLARED alignment histogram, likewise recomputed and cross-checked by the validator. Declaring it is what makes the headline claim ('N scoped, M partial, K unmatched') auditable rather than prose.

assumptions.description: The verification project's own assumption ledger. Every assumption an alignment entry leans on must be declared here; the validator enforces that closure. This is the local mirror of BPO's own first-class `assumptions` discipline.

id.description: Local assumption identifier. The pattern is deliberately generic — no project's prefix is baked into this contract. Uniqueness is enforced in code, not by this pattern.

family.description: Grouping label, e.g. an interface class, an execution platform, or a bounded-model family.

discharged_by.description: External artifact or BPO id discharging this assumption. `null` is meaningful: an explicitly accepted but undischarged hypothesis.

alignments.description: One entry per local obligation. The entry records where the local predicate sits relative to the BPO catalogue, what evidence exists for it locally, and — critically — what the alignment does NOT transfer.

alignment.description: `scoped-instantiation`: the local predicate instantiates one expressly identified BPO clause under stated symbol bindings and assumptions. `partial-overlap`: local and BPO records share a security intent or facet, but neither semantically covers the other. `no-exact-match`: the BPO baseline has no record with the required semantics. The enum deliberately offers no value meaning 'equivalent to' or 'proves' — those readings belong to the core relationship DAG, which a crosswalk does not earn.

bpo_targets.description: BPO records this entry aligns to. Must be empty when `alignment` is `no-exact-match` (that is the whole content of the claim) and non-empty otherwise.

clause.description: The exact generic clause instantiated. Required for a scoped instantiation: 'this property, somewhere' is not a scoped claim.

symbol_bindings.description: Binds each generic parameter the aligned clause quantifies over to its local realization. This is what makes a scoped instantiation checkable rather than asserted.

generic.description: Symbol as named in the BPO record's `formalization.symbols`.

local.description: The local model's realization of it.

uncovered_clauses.description: Clauses of the target record this entry does NOT establish. Recording the residual is the point; an entry that lists none is claiming total coverage and should be read sceptically.

residual_scope.description: Prose statement of what remains outside this entry's scope.

local_assumptions.description: Ids resolving into this document's own `assumptions[]`. Closure enforced by the validator.

evidence.description: The local executable result, if any. `class` states the KIND of evidence obtained; the three claim fields state what is being ASSERTED about its reach. Keeping them separate is what lets the validator reject the common overstatements (operation-local checking reported as reachable, static assertions reported as transition-preserving, a curated trace reported as domain-exhaustive) mechanically instead of editorially.

class.description: The kind of evidence actually produced.

grade.description: Project-local evidence grade. The scale's meaning is the project's to define; BPO only requires that one be stated.

machine.description: The model / machine the result was obtained on.

bounds.description: The finite bounds the result holds within. A bounded result reported without its bounds is not a result.

reachability_claim.description: Whether the state space was covered exhaustively (within bounds), only partially, or not explored at all. Must not be `exhaustive` when `class` is `operation-local-cbc`: constraint-based checking of one operation says nothing about reachability of the states it was checked over.

transition_preservation.description: Whether the result establishes that the property is preserved by transitions. Must be false when `class` is `static-assertion`: an assertion over a state enumeration is not an inductive step.

domain_exhaustive.description: Whether the result covers the whole declared domain. Must be false when `class` is `curated-trace`: a hand-built trace demonstrates reachability of one behaviour, never absence of others.

reproducible.description: Whether the cited artifact actually resolves and the result re-derives from it. Recording `false` honestly is the intended use; omitting the field to avoid saying so is not.

proof_transfer.description: Pinned by schema. An alignment is a semantic mapping, not a refinement proof: it does not transfer a local model-checking result onto the generic BPO record, prove that record, or establish an unbounded claim about a deployed system. Should an independent refinement artifact ever exist, it would be a separate record type — not a relaxation of this field.

review_caveat.description: Any independent-review finding qualifying this entry — e.g. a property found unfalsifiable under the chosen bounds, or a result that did not reproduce. A caveat recorded here is expected to be reflected in `evidence.result`, not to contradict it.
